counterargs.read: The evidence has shifted from 'one soft print' to 'confirmed soft Treasury demand in the Note bucket', and bond vol has validated it -- the grouped risk-off rule (Group A + Group B) is technically met at the Sep 23 close. But the transmission has stopped at the rates layer: credit is flat, funding is flat, equities are giving back modestly rather than breaking. That profile is DURATION REPRICING escalating toward, but not yet at, Treasury intermediation stress. The call is to treat the regime as transitioning (provisional) and let the 7Y today, the H.4.1 tonight and whether MOVE holds above 80 tomorrow decide whether the transition is confirmed or faded.

treasury_auctions.narrative: The 5Y (91282CRN3) settled at 5.033% with the weakest demand profile of its trailing 20: bid-to-cover 2.21 (prior range 2.28-2.42), indirect take 47.0% (prior range 53.2-73.4%), and a 95th-pctile dealer take-down (13.6%) -- materially weaker than August's 5Y (BTC 2.37, indirect 54.3%, dealer 8.9%). Coming right after the soft Sep 22 2Y (indirect 10th pctile, dealer 75th), that is two consecutive soft Note-bucket prints and three soft of the last four auctions, so the module moves Healthy -> EARLY WARNING. Rates repriced ~15bp into the Sep 23 close and MOVE spiked to 95.45, corroborating the auction signal. What keeps this short of TREASURY INTERMEDIATION STRESS: funding is normal (SOFR-IORB -3bp, repo_confirmation false), credit is calm, and no auction has visibly tailed (tail_bps unavailable). So today's read is DURATION REPRICING that has escalated to an early-warning demand problem -- auction_weakness and dealer_pressure true, repo_confirmation false. The 7Y today is the next test; a third weak print plus repo widening would be the path to Intermediation Stress.
